exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Maximum and Minimum Values of a Vertically Translated Sine or Cosine Function

question.text: What is the minimum value of $y=\sin x +3 ?$
question.explanation:
Method 1

To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

  • Start with the graph of $y = \sin x.$

  • Then, shift it by $3$ units up.

The resulting graph is shown below.

From the graph, we see that the minimum value is $y = 2.$

Method 2

We know that $y = \sin{x}$ has a minimum value of $-1.$

\[ -1 \leq \sin x \]

Adding $3$ from both sides of the above inequality gives:

\begin{align*} -1 + 3 & \leq \sin{x} + 3 \\[3pt] 2 & \leq \sin{x} + 3 \end{align*}

Therefore, the minimum value of $\sin{x} + 3$ is $2.$

example.title: Finding the Maximum and Minimum Values of a Vertically Translated Sine or Cosine Function

question.explanation:
Method 1

To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

  • Start with the graph of $y = \sin x.$

  • Then, shift it by $2$ units up.

The resulting graph is shown below.

From the graph, we see that the maximum value is $y = 3.$

Method 2

We know that $y = \sin{x}$ has a maximum value of $1.$

\[ \sin x \leq 1 \]

Adding $2$ to both sides of the above inequality gives:

\begin{align*} \sin{x} + 2 & \leq 1 + 2\\[3pt] \sin{x} + 2 & \leq 3 \end{align*}

Therefore, the maximum value of $\sin{x} + 2$ is $3.$

example.title: Finding the Maximum and Minimum Values of a Vertically Translated Sine or Cosine Function

question.explanation:
Method 1

To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

  • Start with the graph of $y = \cos x.$

  • Then, shift it by $1$ unit up.

The resulting graph is shown below.

From the graph, we see that the maximum value is $y = 2.$

Method 2

We know that $y = \cos{x}$ has a maximum value of $1.$

\[ \cos{x} \leq 1 \]

Adding $1$ to both sides of the above inequality gives:

\begin{align*} \cos{x} + 1 \leq 1 + 1\\[3pt] \cos{x} + 1 \leq 2 \end{align*}

Therefore, the maximum value of $\cos{x} + 1$ is $2.$

example.title: Finding the Maximum and Minimum Values of a Vertically Translated Sine or Cosine Function

question.explanation:
Method 1

To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

  • Start with the graph of $y = \sin x.$

  • Then, shift it by $2$ units down.

The resulting graph is shown below.

From the graph, we see that the minimum value is $y = -3.$

Method 2

We know that $y = \sin{x}$ has a minimum value of $-1.$

\[ -1 \leq \sin x \]

Subtracting $2$ from both sides of the above inequality gives:

\begin{align*} -1 - 2 & \leq \sin{x} - 2 \\[3pt] -3 & \leq \sin{x} - 2 \end{align*}

Therefore, the minimum value of $\sin{x} - 2$ is $-3.$

exampleAnswers.title: The Equation of a Vertically Translated Tangent Function

question.text: The graph above shows $y=\tan{x}+D.$ What is the value of $D?$
question.explanation:
To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

  • Start with the graph of $y = \tan x.$

  • Then, shift it by $1.5$ units down.

Therefore, the given curve is the graph of $y = \tan x - 1.5.$ Thus, $D = -1.5.$
